routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: First climbed by Hornbein and Unsoeld in 1963 via the West Shoulder and the exposed West Ridge. One of the great achievements in Himalayan climbing. The route traverses above the Western Cwm before committing to the ridge at 7700m, with no retreat possible once committed.
routes.hazards: ["Extreme exposure on ridge","No retreat once committed","Cornices","High altitude","Wind loading"]

tips.content: This is a committing line with no easy descent once on the ridge proper above 7700m
Most parties descend via the South Col route making this a traverse of the mountain
Requires exceptional fitness and altitude tolerance as the ridge is long and exposed

gear.notes: For fixing the exposed ridge sections
Anchors on the corniced ridge sections

reviews.title: The ultimate Everest line
reviews.body: After weeks of preparation and load carries, our team committed to the ridge. The exposure above the Rongbuk is staggering. Once past the point of no return there is only up. Descended the South Col route completing the traverse. A once in a lifetime achievement.
reviews.conditions: Brief weather window, moderate winds on ridge, clear summit day

routes.summary: A legendary traverse route pioneered by Hornbein and Unsoeld in 1963, committing to the exposed West Ridge above 7700m with no retreat possible.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $11,000 per climber. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer assigned by government.
routes.safetyNotes: Once committed to the ridge above 7700m there is no viable retreat; most parties descend the South Col route. Extreme wind loading creates dangerous cornices along the entire ridge. Supplemental oxygen is strongly recommended given the sustained time above 8000m. Communication with South Col teams is essential for descent logistics.

routes.name: Southwest Face
routes.description: The massive southwest face was first climbed by a British expedition led by Chris Bonington in 1975. The route tackles the Rock Band at 8200m, one of the greatest obstacles in Himalayan climbing. A serious big wall objective at extreme altitude requiring siege tactics.
routes.hazards: ["Rock Band at 8200m","Avalanche risk on face","Extreme altitude technical climbing","Rockfall","Storms trapping climbers high"]

tips.content: The Rock Band is the crux and requires aid climbing at nearly 8300m
Siege style with multiple camps on the face is the only realistic approach

gear.notes: For the Rock Band at 8200m
gear.specificProduct: Black Diamond Camalot C4 Full Set + Aiders

links.productName: Black Diamond Camalot C4 Full Rack
Black Diamond Big Wall Rack Package

gear.notes: For bivouacs on the steep face
gear.specificProduct: Black Diamond Cliff Cabana Double Portaledge

reviews.title: Himalayan big wall at its finest
reviews.body: Months of effort culminated in breaching the Rock Band. The scale of the southwest face is incomprehensible from base camp. Every pitch above 8000m felt like a major achievement. This route separates expedition mountaineering from everything else.
reviews.conditions: Variable weather, snow on face, cold temperatures throughout

routes.summary: A massive big-wall objective at extreme altitude, requiring siege tactics to breach the notorious Rock Band at 8200m on Everest's imposing southwest face.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $11,000 per climber. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer assigned by government.
routes.safetyNotes: The Rock Band at 8200m requires aid climbing at extreme altitude where cognitive impairment is severe. Avalanche risk on the open face is constant and unpredictable. Siege-style logistics with multiple camps require large experienced teams. Retreat from the upper face in storm conditions may be impossible.

routes.name: Hornbein Couloir
routes.description: The steep couloir splitting the North Face, first climbed by Tom Hornbein during the 1963 West Ridge expedition. A direct and aesthetic line offering steep snow and mixed climbing to the upper West Ridge. Rarely repeated due to objective hazards and extreme altitude.
routes.hazards: ["Steep ice and mixed terrain at extreme altitude","Avalanche risk in couloir","Rockfall","No easy escape"]

tips.content: Conditions in the couloir vary enormously year to year, extensive reconnaissance is essential
The couloir funnels all debris from above, move through exposed sections quickly

gear.notes: Steep ice sections in the couloir require aggressive tools
For protection on sustained steep ice

reviews.title: A historic line
reviews.body: The couloir is a direct slash up the North Face that draws the eye from base camp. Climbing steep ice at 7500m with the exposure of the North Face below is an out of body experience. Very few teams have repeated this route and for good reason.
reviews.conditions: Good ice in couloir, stable weather window, cold

routes.summary: A rare and direct couloir line splitting Everest's North Face, offering steep snow and mixed climbing to the upper West Ridge at extreme altitude.
routes.permitInfo: Chinese Tibet Mountaineering Association (CTMA) permit required. Fee approximately $9,950 per climber for a team of 7+. Must book through authorized Chinese operator. Apply at least 8 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The couloir funnels all rockfall and spindrift from the upper face, making timing through exposed sections critical. Conditions vary enormously between years and extensive reconnaissance is essential. Very few successful ascents have been made due to the extreme objective hazards. Descent is typically via the North Ridge standard route.

routes.name: East Face (Kangshung Face)
routes.description: The remote and massive east face rising above the Kangshung Glacier in Tibet. First climbed in 1983 by an American team. The approach alone requires days of difficult glacier travel. The face is threatened by enormous hanging seracs and avalanches, making it one of the most dangerous routes on Everest.
routes.hazards: ["Massive serac barriers","Constant avalanche threat","Remote approach","Extreme altitude","No rescue possible"]

tips.content: The Kangshung approach is extremely remote with no infrastructure or support
Serac activity on this face is unpredictable and potentially catastrophic

gear.notes: No other communication is possible from the Kangshung side
Self-sufficient medical capability is essential given remoteness

links.productName: Adventure Medical Kits Mountain Series Guide
Adventure Medical Kits Mountain Medic Kit

reviews.title: The wildest side of Everest
reviews.body: The Kangshung Face is Everest at its most raw and unforgiving. The approach through the glacier maze took days. The face itself is constantly alive with avalanches. Climbing through the night to avoid serac exposure was terrifying. Only for teams seeking the ultimate challenge.
reviews.conditions: Unstable seracs, brief stable weather, deep snow on face

routes.summary: The most remote and dangerous route on Everest, ascending the massive east face above the Kangshung Glacier with enormous hanging seracs and constant avalanche threat.
routes.permitInfo: Chinese Tibet Mountaineering Association (CTMA) permit required. Fee approximately $9,950 per climber. Kangshung approach requires special access permission. Apply through authorized Chinese operator at least 10 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The Kangshung side is extremely remote with no infrastructure, no other teams, and no rescue capability. Massive serac barriers pose catastrophic and unpredictable collapse risk. A satellite phone is the only communication option. The multi-day glacier approach adds significant logistical complexity.

routes.name: South Pillar
routes.description: A line on the south face right of the Southwest Face route, following a prominent rock pillar. Requires sustained technical climbing at extreme altitude. First climbed by a Polish expedition. The pillar offers more protection from avalanche than the open face but demands high-standard rock climbing above 7500m.
routes.hazards: ["Technical rock at extreme altitude","Rockfall","Storm exposure on pillar","Altitude sickness"]

tips.content: Rock climbing skills to UIAA V are needed at altitudes above 7500m
The pillar provides a more logical and protected line than the open southwest face

gear.notes: Rock protection needed for the pillar pitches at altitude
gear.specificProduct: Black Diamond Camalot C4 Rack Pack

links.productName: Black Diamond Camalot C4 Rack Pack
Black Diamond C4 Cam Full Set

gear.notes: For ferrying supplies up the multi-day pillar

reviews.title: Technical Himalayan climbing at its hardest
reviews.body: The South Pillar demands rock climbing ability at altitudes where simply breathing is a struggle. Pulling moves on cold granite at 8000m is surreal. The pillar line is elegant from below but punishing to climb. For elite alpinists only.
reviews.conditions: Dry rock on lower pillar, mixed above 7800m, cold

routes.summary: A demanding rock pillar on Everest's south face requiring sustained high-standard technical climbing above 7500m, first climbed by a Polish expedition.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $11,000 per climber. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer assigned by government.
routes.safetyNotes: Rock climbing to UIAA V is required at altitudes above 7500m where physical and cognitive performance is severely impaired. Rockfall from the pillar is a constant hazard. Hauling supplies up the multi-day route demands large team logistics. Retreat from the upper pillar is extremely difficult.

routes.name: North Face Direct
routes.description: A direct line up the center of the massive North Face above the Rongbuk Glacier. Involves steep mixed climbing on the Great Couloir and headwall. One of the most committing lines on Everest with sustained difficulties at extreme altitude and no easy retreat options.
routes.hazards: ["Sustained technical difficulty at altitude","Rockfall in Great Couloir","Wind exposure","No retreat from upper face"]

tips.content: The Great Couloir channels rockfall and spindrift, timing through it is critical
Acclimatization on the standard North Ridge route before attempting the face is advisable

gear.notes: Technical mixed terrain on the headwall demands specialized tools
Planned bivouacs on the face require minimal but adequate shelter

reviews.title: The ultimate north face
reviews.body: The scale of Everest's North Face is hard to convey. Climbing directly up the center feels like climbing a frozen skyscraper. The Great Couloir is a natural highway for debris. We moved fast and were rewarded with stable conditions on the headwall. Descended the standard route completely spent.
reviews.conditions: Cold and clear, light wind on face, some spindrift

routes.summary: A direct and committing line up the center of Everest's massive North Face, featuring steep mixed climbing through the Great Couloir and headwall.
routes.permitInfo: Chinese Tibet Mountaineering Association (CTMA) permit required. Fee approximately $9,950 per climber for a team of 7+. Must book through authorized Chinese operator. Apply at least 8 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The Great Couloir channels rockfall and spindrift making timing through it absolutely critical. No retreat is possible from the upper face in deteriorating conditions. Prior acclimatization on the standard North Ridge route is strongly advised. Planned bivouacs on the face require ultralight but reliable shelter systems.

routes.name: North Ridge (Chinese Route)
routes.description: The route from the Chinese side via the K2 Glacier and the long North Ridge. First climbed by a Chinese-Japanese expedition in 1982. Less popular than the Abruzzi but avoids the Bottleneck serac. The ridge is long and exposed with sustained mixed terrain above 7500m.
routes.hazards: ["Long exposed ridge","Wind loading","Cornices","Remote approach from China","Permit difficulties"]

tips.content: Chinese permits for K2 are harder to obtain and more expensive than Pakistani permits
The north side is more remote with less infrastructure than the Pakistani side
The ridge is very long and requires multiple camps to be established

gear.notes: For anchoring camps and fixed lines on the snow ridge
The north side is significantly colder due to wind exposure

links.productName: Mountain Hardwear Absolute Zero Down Suit

reviews.title: K2 from the quiet side
reviews.body: The north side of K2 is a completely different experience from the crowded Abruzzi. The ridge is long and committing but avoids the terrifying Bottleneck. Chinese base camp is remote and austere. The summit feels more earned from this side.
reviews.conditions: Variable winds on ridge, clear summit window, very cold

routes.summary: A long and exposed ridge route on K2's Chinese side, avoiding the deadly Bottleneck serac but demanding sustained mixed climbing above 7500m.
routes.permitInfo: Chinese Mountaineering Association (CMA) permit required. Fee approximately $13,000-$18,000 per climber. Chinese permits are harder to obtain and require booking through an authorized Chinese operator at least 12 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Chinese-side access is more remote with significantly less infrastructure than the Pakistani side. The ridge is extremely long and requires multiple well-stocked camps. Wind loading creates dangerous cornices along the entire ridge. Permit logistics from China add substantial lead time and cost.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: A challenging route up K2's western flank first attempted in 1974 and completed in 1981. The route follows a mixed terrain ridge with significant rockfall danger and technical climbing at high altitude. Less frequented than the Abruzzi with fewer fixed ropes.
routes.hazards: ["Rockfall","Mixed technical climbing","Limited fixed ropes","Isolation from other teams"]

tips.content: The lower ridge has serious rockfall danger, move through quickly in early morning
Less infrastructure means your team must be fully self-sufficient

gear.notes: Mixed rock and ice sections require a versatile rack
Must bring your own as there are few existing fixed lines

reviews.title: A lonely line on K2
reviews.body: The west ridge sees almost no traffic compared to the Abruzzi. Our team was alone on the entire route. The mixed climbing at 7000m was serious and the rockfall on the lower sections kept us moving fast. K2 at its most remote.
reviews.conditions: Mixed rock and ice, occasional rockfall, brief summit window

routes.summary: A challenging and isolated route on K2's western flank with significant rockfall danger and technical mixed climbing, seeing very little traffic.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $7,200 per climber for K2. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The lower ridge has serious rockfall danger requiring early morning movement. Your team must be fully self-sufficient as there are few if any other teams on this route. Limited fixed ropes mean the team must bring and install all their own. Isolation from other teams means no external rescue capability.

routes.name: Cesen Route (South-Southwest Ridge)
routes.description: A direct line on the south-southwest face claimed by Tomo Cesen in 1986 though the ascent is disputed. The route has since been climbed confirmed by other teams. It offers a more direct line to the shoulder than the Abruzzi, avoiding the Black Pyramid but with sustained steep snow and ice.
routes.hazards: ["Steep sustained snow and ice","Avalanche risk on face","Serac danger","Wind exposure on shoulder"]

tips.content: The face receives heavy spindrift loading, timing between storm cycles is critical
Joins the Abruzzi route at the shoulder for the final push to the summit

gear.notes: Sustained steep ice requires aggressive modern tools
Protection for the steep ice face

reviews.title: Direct and sustained
reviews.body: The Cesen line is more direct than the Abruzzi and avoids the Black Pyramid rockfall. The face is sustained at 50-55 degrees for thousands of feet. Joining the Abruzzi at the shoulder for the Bottleneck was a rude welcome. A serious alternative route.
reviews.conditions: Good ice conditions, some wind loading, cold

routes.summary: A direct line on K2's south-southwest face with sustained steep snow and ice, bypassing the Black Pyramid but joining the Abruzzi at the deadly Bottleneck.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $7,200 per climber for K2. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The face receives heavy spindrift loading between storm cycles making timing critical. Sustained 50-55 degree ice for thousands of feet demands excellent front-pointing endurance. The route joins the Abruzzi at the shoulder, exposing climbers to the Bottleneck serac. Serac danger on the face itself adds objective risk.

routes.name: Magic Line (South-Southwest Pillar)
routes.description: One of the hardest routes on any 8000m peak, climbing the south-southwest pillar directly. First climbed in 1986 by a Polish-Slovak team at tremendous cost. The route involves extreme technical difficulty at altitude with no retreat options from the upper pillar.
routes.hazards: ["Extreme technical difficulty at altitude","No retreat from upper pillar","Rockfall","Storm exposure","UIAA VI climbing above 7000m"]

tips.content: This route has seen very few ascents and multiple fatalities, only for elite alpinists
The pillar demands rock climbing skills well into the UIAA VI range at over 7000m

gear.notes: Technical rock features require a complete trad and aid rack
gear.specificProduct: Black Diamond Big Wall Rack Package

links.productName: Black Diamond Complete Big Wall Kit

gear.notes: Multi-day commitment on the vertical pillar requires hanging bivouacs
gear.specificProduct: Black Diamond Cliff Cabana Double Portaledge

reviews.title: The hardest line on the hardest mountain
reviews.body: The Magic Line is alpinism pushed to the absolute limit. Technical rock climbing at over 7000m where every move requires concentration. The pillar is a vertical world of its own. Only a handful of teams have succeeded and the mountain has taken a heavy toll. Not to be underestimated.
reviews.conditions: Brief stable window, cold rock, mixed conditions on upper pillar

routes.summary: One of the hardest routes on any 8000m peak, climbing K2's south-southwest pillar with extreme technical difficulty and no retreat from the upper sections.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $7,200 per climber for K2. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: This route has seen very few ascents and multiple fatalities; it is exclusively for elite alpinists. UIAA VI rock climbing above 7000m demands extraordinary fitness and acclimatization. No retreat is possible from the upper pillar once committed. The 1986 first ascent came at tremendous human cost.

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.description: A long and complex ridge route starting from the Savoia Glacier on the northwest side. The ridge offers varied terrain including rock towers, snow aretes, and mixed gullies. First climbed in 1991. Less threatened by seracs than the Abruzzi but extremely long and committing.
routes.hazards: ["Extremely long ridge","Rock towers requiring technical climbing","Cornices","Wind exposure","Logistical complexity"]

tips.content: The ridge requires navigating multiple rock towers which add time and complexity
Establish at least 4 camps along the ridge for a realistic summit bid

gear.notes: For the rock tower sections along the ridge
Long ridge requires extensive fixing for load carries

reviews.title: The endless ridge
reviews.body: The northwest ridge of K2 goes on forever. Each time you think the summit is close another rock tower appears. The climbing is varied and interesting but the sheer length is the real challenge. We spent five weeks establishing camps before our summit bid.
reviews.conditions: Variable weather, wind on exposed sections, good rock on towers

routes.summary: An extremely long and complex ridge route on K2 featuring rock towers, snow aretes, and mixed gullies, demanding weeks of effort to establish camps.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $7,200 per climber for K2. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The ridge requires navigating multiple rock towers which add significant time and technical complexity. At least four camps must be established along the ridge for a realistic summit bid. Cornices on the leeward side are enormous and require constant vigilance. The sheer length means extended time at high altitude with associated deterioration risk.

routes.name: Southwest Face (Normal Route)
routes.description: The most frequently climbed route on the world's third highest peak, first ascended by a British team in 1955. The route ascends from the Yalung Glacier via the Great Shelf and upper southwest face. Tradition holds that climbers stop a few feet below the actual summit out of respect for local beliefs.
routes.hazards: ["Avalanche risk on face","Extreme altitude","Crevassed glacier approach","Cornices on summit ridge","Unpredictable weather"]

tips.content: Most climbers honor the tradition of stopping short of the true summit by a few meters
The Great Shelf at 7400m is a key landmark and site for high camp
Spring season from April to May provides the best weather windows

gear.notes: Essential above 7500m where temperatures are extreme

links.productName: Mountain Hardwear Absolute Zero Down Suit

gear.notes: Many commercial expeditions use oxygen above Camp 4
Sections of the face require fixed ropes for safety

reviews.title: Sacred giant of the Himalayas
reviews.body: Kangchenjunga is a massive and serious mountain that receives far less traffic than Everest. The southwest face route is long but logical. Stopping short of the summit was a meaningful moment. The mountain demands deep respect.
reviews.conditions: Stable spring weather, moderate wind, deep snow above 7000m

routes.summary: The most frequented route on the world's third highest peak, ascending via the Yalung Glacier and Great Shelf with a tradition of stopping just below the true summit.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Liaison officer required. Apply at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Most climbers honor the tradition of stopping a few meters short of the true summit out of respect for local Sikkimese beliefs. Avalanche risk on the face is significant especially during and after snowfall. The Great Shelf at 7400m is exposed to wind and provides the high camp location. Crevasse danger on the Yalung Glacier approach requires roped travel.

routes.name: North Face
routes.description: A direct line up the imposing north face from the Kangchenjunga Glacier in Nepal. The face is massive and threatened by ice avalanches. First climbed in 1977 by an Indian military expedition. Rarely attempted due to extreme objective danger.
routes.hazards: ["Ice avalanches","Extreme altitude","Steep mixed terrain","Remote approach","Serac collapse"]

tips.content: Serac activity on the north face is unpredictable, timing exposure to hanging ice is critical
The approach from the north requires trekking through remote Nepali valleys

gear.notes: Steep ice sections demand aggressive modern tools
Extensive steep ice requires solid protection

reviews.title: One of the great Himalayan faces
reviews.body: The north face of Kangchenjunga is a wall of ice and rock on a scale that defies description. The constant rumble of seracs is unsettling. We threaded a line through the danger zones moving fast when exposed. Reaching the summit ridge felt like escaping a war zone.
reviews.conditions: Active seracs, cold temperatures, brief stable window

routes.summary: A massive and rarely attempted direct line on Kangchenjunga's north face, threatened by constant ice avalanches and serac collapse from hanging glaciers.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Liaison officer required. Apply at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Serac activity on the north face is entirely unpredictable and potentially catastrophic. The approach requires trekking through remote Nepali valleys with limited support infrastructure. Steep mixed terrain at extreme altitude demands exceptional fitness. Very few teams have attempted this face and the objective hazard profile is extreme.

routes.name: Northeast Spur
routes.description: A prominent spur on the northeast side of the mountain approached from the Zemu Glacier in Sikkim, India. First climbed in 1977. The route offers a more direct line to the summit than the southwest face but involves significant technical mixed climbing at altitude.
routes.hazards: ["Mixed technical climbing","Rockfall on spur","Altitude","Indian permit restrictions","Crevassed approach"]

tips.content: Access from the Indian side through Sikkim requires special permits and coordination
The Zemu Glacier approach is remote and beautiful but adds several days to the expedition

gear.notes: The spur features extensive rock and ice mixed terrain
gear.specificProduct: Black Diamond Mixed Climbing Rack Package

gear.notes: Multiple high camps needed on the spur

reviews.title: The Indian approach to Kangchenjunga
reviews.body: Approaching from Sikkim adds a cultural dimension to the climb. The Zemu Glacier is stunning. The northeast spur is technical and sustained with excellent mixed climbing. Views into Sikkim from the upper spur are unmatched.
reviews.conditions: Dry rock on lower spur, icy mixed terrain above 7000m

routes.summary: A prominent spur approached from the scenic Zemu Glacier in Sikkim, India, offering direct mixed climbing to Kangchenjunga's summit with special permit requirements.
routes.permitInfo: Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF) permit required, plus special Sikkim Inner Line Permit. Fee approximately $2,000 per climber. Coordination with Indian military may be required. Apply at least 6 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Access from the Indian side through Sikkim requires special permits and coordination with Indian authorities. The Zemu Glacier approach is remote and adds several days. Mixed rock and ice terrain on the spur demands versatile climbing skills. Crevassed approach glacier requires careful roped travel.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: A long ridge route from the south approaching via the Yalung Glacier. The ridge is less steep than the face routes but extremely long and exposed. Technical difficulties are moderate but the sustained altitude and distance make it a serious undertaking.
routes.hazards: ["Extreme length","Cornices","Wind exposure","Altitude","Logistical challenges with camps"]

tips.content: The ridge is very long and requires patience and careful camp placement
Cornices can be massive on the leeward side of the ridge, stay well back from the edge

gear.notes: For probing cornice edges on the long ridge
Long ridge requires extensive marking for descent in poor visibility

reviews.title: Marathon ridge at altitude
reviews.body: The south ridge of Kangchenjunga is a test of endurance rather than technical ability. Day after day of ridge walking at 7000m plus. The cornices are enormous and demand constant vigilance. Beautiful but exhausting.
reviews.conditions: Wind on ridge, clear views, cold nights at camps

routes.summary: An extremely long ridge route from the Yalung Glacier requiring exceptional endurance at altitude, with massive cornices demanding constant vigilance.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Liaison officer required. Apply at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The ridge is extremely long and tests endurance rather than technical skill at altitude. Cornices on the leeward side can be massive and collapse without warning. Extensive wanding is required for safe descent navigation in poor visibility. Multiple camps must be placed along the ridge adding logistical complexity.

routes.name: Yalung Face
routes.description: The south-facing wall above the Yalung Glacier. A massive face with multiple possible lines through icefalls and rock bands. The face receives sun exposure which increases avalanche risk but also provides warmer climbing conditions. First climbed by a Japanese expedition.
routes.hazards: ["Sun-triggered avalanches","Icefall zones","Rock bands","Altitude","Rapid condition changes"]

tips.content: Climb the face in the early morning hours before sun loosens the snow
Multiple lines are possible through the icefalls, scout carefully from base camp

gear.notes: Sun-exposed face has high avalanche risk
Steep ice through the icefall sections

reviews.title: A face of immense scale
reviews.body: The Yalung Face is one of the most impressive walls in the Himalayas. The sun exposure creates beautiful climbing conditions but also deadly avalanche risk. Threading through the icefall in pre-dawn darkness was nerve-wracking. The scale overwhelms.
reviews.conditions: Pre-dawn start essential, afternoon avalanches, mixed conditions

routes.summary: A massive south-facing wall above the Yalung Glacier with multiple line options through icefalls, where sun exposure creates both warmer conditions and serious avalanche risk.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Liaison officer required. Apply at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Sun exposure on this south-facing wall triggers afternoon avalanches making early morning climbs essential. Multiple possible lines through the icefalls should be carefully scouted from base camp. Icefall zones present unpredictable serac collapse hazards. Rapid condition changes from solar warming require constant reassessment.

routes.name: West Face (Normal Route)
routes.description: The standard route shares the Everest South Col approach through the Khumbu Icefall and Western Cwm before branching left at Camp 3 to traverse the Lhotse Face directly to the summit couloir. The final couloir is steep and often icy with exposure to rockfall.
routes.hazards: ["Khumbu Icefall","Steep summit couloir","Rockfall","Altitude","Icy conditions on face"]

tips.content: The summit couloir is often hard blue ice requiring front-pointing skills
Many teams combine a Lhotse attempt with an Everest permit since the approach is shared
The Lhotse Face above Camp 3 is steep and requires fixed ropes

gear.notes: Hard ice on the Lhotse Face and summit couloir requires stiff crampons
Recommended for the summit push above 8000m
Technical ice in the summit couloir

reviews.title: In the shadow of Everest
reviews.body: Lhotse shares the Everest approach but feels like a different mountain above Camp 3. The Lhotse Face is brutally steep and the summit couloir is a serious piece of ice climbing at altitude. Far fewer climbers than Everest which adds to the experience.
reviews.conditions: Hard ice on face, clear weather, light wind

routes.summary: The standard route sharing Everest's approach through the Khumbu Icefall before branching to Lhotse's steep summit couloir, often hard blue ice requiring strong front-pointing.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members). Many teams combine with an Everest permit. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 6 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The summit couloir is often hard blue ice requiring strong front-pointing technique and reliable crampon skills. The Khumbu Icefall is an unavoidable objective hazard with moving seracs. Rockfall in the summit couloir is a significant danger especially in afternoon warmth. Many teams combine Lhotse with Everest permits since the approach is shared.

routes.name: South Face
routes.description: The 3000m south face of Lhotse is one of the last great problems in Himalayan climbing, not successfully climbed until 1990 by a Soviet team. The face is massive, steep, and constantly threatened by rockfall and ice avalanches. Considered by many to be the hardest route on any 8000m peak.
routes.hazards: ["Extreme technical difficulty","Constant rockfall","Avalanche risk","3000m of sustained climbing","No escape from upper face"]

tips.content: This face has repelled many of the worlds best alpinists over decades of attempts
Night climbing is essential to avoid rockfall triggered by solar warming

gear.notes: Mixed rock and ice requires comprehensive protection
Multiple forced bivouacs on the face

reviews.title: The last great problem
reviews.body: The south face of Lhotse is a 3000m wall that has humbled generations of alpinists. The scale is difficult to comprehend from below. Every meter gained feels like a major achievement. This is Himalayan climbing at its absolute limit.
reviews.conditions: Cold and dry, some rockfall, stable weather window

routes.summary: One of the most difficult routes on any 8000m peak, with 3000m of sustained technical climbing on a face that repelled the world's best alpinists for decades.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members). Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer required.
routes.safetyNotes: This face has repelled many of the world's best alpinists over decades and claimed several lives. Night climbing is essential to minimize rockfall triggered by solar warming. The 3000m of sustained climbing offers no escape from the upper face. Multiple forced bivouacs on the face are virtually guaranteed.

routes.name: Lhotse Couloir (North Face)
routes.description: A prominent couloir on the north side of Lhotse visible from the Everest approach. The couloir offers a more direct line than the standard route but with steeper sustained ice climbing. Access is from the Western Cwm shared with the Everest approach.
routes.hazards: ["Steep sustained ice","Rockfall in couloir","Spindrift avalanches","Altitude"]

gear.notes: Sustained 50-60 degree ice in the couloir
Long pitches of steep ice require good protection

reviews.title: Direct and committing
reviews.body: The Lhotse Couloir is visible from the Everest trail and draws the eye. Climbing it is as committing as it looks. Sustained steep ice for hundreds of meters with debris funneling from above. A proper alpine challenge at 8000m.
reviews.conditions: Good ice, cold morning starts, some spindrift

routes.summary: A prominent couloir on Lhotse's north side visible from the Everest approach, offering steeper and more direct ice climbing than the standard route.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members). Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 6 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The couloir funnels all debris from above making timing through exposed sections critical. Sustained 50-60 degree ice requires solid front-pointing endurance. Early morning starts are essential to minimize spindrift and rockfall exposure. Access from the Western Cwm shares the Khumbu Icefall hazard.

routes.name: Normal Route (Northwest Ridge)
routes.description: The standard route on the world's fifth highest peak via the Makalu La and northwest ridge. First climbed by a French expedition in 1955. The approach through the Barun Valley is spectacular. The upper ridge involves steep mixed terrain and the famous rock step at 8200m.

The rock step at 8200m is the crux and requires UIAA III climbing at extreme altitude
Spring offers the best weather with May being prime summit month

Some climbers change footwear for the rock step

reviews.title: The most beautiful 8000er
reviews.body: Makalu's perfect pyramid shape makes it arguably the most beautiful 8000m peak. The northwest ridge is a classic alpine route at extreme altitude. The rock step at 8200m is a memorable crux. The Barun Valley approach is worth the trip alone.
reviews.conditions: Clear May weather, moderate wind on ridge, good rock on step

routes.summary: The standard route on the world's fifth highest peak via the Makalu La, featuring a spectacular Barun Valley approach and a famous rock step at 8200m.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The rock step at 8200m requires UIAA III climbing at extreme altitude where cognitive function is severely impaired. The Barun Valley approach is remote with limited rescue options adding 5-6 trekking days. Wind on the exposed northwest ridge can be extreme and unpredictable. Avalanche danger on the approach glacier requires careful route finding.

routes.name: West Pillar
routes.description: A direct line up the massive west pillar first climbed in 1971 by a French team. The pillar rises over 2500m from the glacier with sustained technical climbing on rock and mixed terrain. One of the great classic Himalayan routes.
routes.hazards: ["Sustained technical climbing","Rockfall","Storm exposure","No easy retreat","Altitude"]

Rock quality on the pillar is generally good granite but loose sections exist

reviews.title: A Himalayan classic
reviews.body: The west pillar of Makalu is one of the great routes of the Himalayas. The pillar rises like a cathedral spire from the glacier. Technical climbing at altitude with incredible exposure. The French first ascent was a masterpiece of alpine style.
reviews.conditions: Mixed conditions, good granite on lower pillar, icy above 7500m

routes.summary: A classic Himalayan route rising 2500m up Makalu's massive west pillar, demanding sustained technical rock and mixed climbing in a siege-style commitment.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The 2500m pillar demands multi-day siege tactics with extensive gear hauling. Rock quality is generally good granite but loose sections pose rockfall hazard. Storm exposure on the exposed pillar can trap teams for days. No easy retreat is possible from the upper sections of the pillar.

routes.name: West Face Direct
routes.description: A direct line up the center of the west face avoiding the pillar. Steeper and more sustained than the West Pillar route with serious objective hazards. The face is swept by avalanches and rockfall making speed essential.
routes.hazards: ["Avalanche risk","Rockfall","Steep sustained face","Altitude","Storm exposure"]

tips.content: Speed is essential on this face as exposure to objective hazards is constant
Alpine style is the only realistic approach given the objective dangers

gear.notes: Fast and light approach requires minimal shelter
Steep ice and mixed terrain throughout

reviews.title: Speed climbing a Himalayan face
reviews.body: The west face direct demands commitment and speed. We climbed fast and light over 3 days. The face is alive with rockfall and spindrift. No time to rest or second-guess. This is alpinism at its most intense.
reviews.conditions: Cold and clear, active face, good ice conditions

routes.summary: A steep and dangerous direct line up Makalu's west face requiring alpine-style speed to minimize exposure to constant avalanche and rockfall hazards.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Speed is the primary safety strategy as exposure to objective hazards is constant on this face. Alpine style is the only realistic approach given the unrelenting avalanche and rockfall danger. The face is alive with activity during daytime warming. Multiple bivouacs on the sustained face are unavoidable.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.description: An alternative ridge route approaching from the east side. The ridge is long and involves several rock gendarmes requiring technical climbing. Less frequented than the northwest ridge but offers a more varied climbing experience.
routes.hazards: ["Rock gendarmes","Cornices","Wind exposure","Remote approach","Technical mixed climbing"]

Eastern approach is less traveled and requires more self-sufficiency

gear.notes: For the gendarme sections on the ridge
For camp and fixed line anchors on the snow ridge

reviews.title: Makalu from the back side
reviews.body: The southeast ridge offers a wilder and more remote experience than the normal route. The rock gendarmes are engaging at altitude and break up the monotony of snow plodding. A fine alternative for experienced Himalayan climbers.
reviews.conditions: Mixed conditions on ridge, some wind, clear summit day

routes.summary: An alternative ridge route on Makalu's eastern side featuring engaging rock gendarmes at altitude, offering a wilder and more remote experience than the normal route.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Rock gendarmes can be turned on their flanks but this adds time and complexity to the route. The eastern approach is less traveled requiring greater self-sufficiency. Cornices along the ridge require careful assessment and probing. Wind exposure on the ridge can be extreme and sustained.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge (Normal Route)
routes.description: The standard route on the world's seventh highest peak approached via the French Col and Northeast Ridge. First climbed in 1960 by a Swiss expedition that famously used an aircraft to establish base camp. The ridge is long and exposed with the notorious Eiger section at 7400m.
routes.hazards: ["Wind on northeast ridge","The Eiger section at 7400m","Crevassed approach","Avalanche on lower slopes","Extreme altitude"]

tips.content: The northeast col can be reached from the Hidden Valley or via the French Col
The Eiger section at 7400m is a steep rock and ice step that is the routes crux
Dhaulagiri has a notoriously fickle weather pattern, patience is essential

gear.notes: The ridge is extremely wind exposed and cold

links.productName: Mountain Hardwear Absolute Zero Down Suit

gear.notes: Fixed ropes on the Eiger section and upper ridge
Used by many commercial teams above Camp 3

reviews.title: The White Mountain
reviews.body: Dhaulagiri is a massive and impressive mountain that dominates the skyline. The northeast ridge is a long and committing route with the Eiger section providing genuine challenge. Wind was our biggest enemy. The summit panorama including Annapurna across the valley is spectacular.
reviews.conditions: Windy ridge, clear summit day, deep snow in places

routes.summary: The standard route on the White Mountain featuring the notorious Eiger section at 7400m and approached via the French Col, with notoriously unpredictable weather.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The Eiger section at 7400m is the technical crux requiring steep mixed climbing on fixed ropes. Dhaulagiri has notoriously fickle weather and patience waiting for a window is essential. The northeast ridge is extremely wind-exposed making windproof layering critical. Crevasse danger on the approach glacier requires roped travel.

routes.name: South Face
routes.description: The massive south face of Dhaulagiri rises over 3500m from the Myagdi Khola valley. First climbed by a Japanese expedition in 1978. The face features steep ice fields, rock bands, and constant avalanche threat. One of the great south faces of the Himalayas.

Multiple lines exist through the face, study conditions carefully from base camp

gear.notes: South face has extreme avalanche exposure
Steep ice fields require aggressive technical tools

reviews.title: One of the great Himalayan faces
reviews.body: The south face of Dhaulagiri is absolutely enormous. Climbing through the night to avoid avalanche exposure was exhausting but essential. The ice fields are sustained and steep. Reaching the summit ridge from the face felt like emerging from another world.
reviews.conditions: Night climbing, stable weather, hard ice on face

routes.summary: A massive 3500m south face rising from the Myagdi Khola valley, demanding night climbing to avoid sun-triggered avalanches on steep ice fields and rock bands.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The south face receives afternoon sun triggering massive avalanches; climbing through the night is essential. Multiple lines exist through the face and must be studied carefully from base camp. Steep ice fields are sustained for thousands of feet requiring excellent endurance. Storm cycles can pin teams down on the face with no escape.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.description: An alternative ridge route from the southwest approached from the Dhaulagiri Icefall. The ridge offers a more sheltered line than the northeast ridge but with more technical mixed climbing. Less frequently attempted.
routes.hazards: ["Dhaulagiri Icefall approach","Mixed climbing on ridge","Cornices","Altitude"]

tips.content: The Dhaulagiri Icefall is dangerous and must be navigated quickly
The ridge offers more shelter from wind than the standard northeast ridge

gear.notes: Varied terrain on the ridge requires versatile gear

reviews.title: Dhaulagiri less traveled
reviews.body: The southwest ridge sees very little traffic which added to the adventure. The Dhaulagiri Icefall approach is intimidating but the ridge itself is a fine mountaineering route. Mixed terrain keeps things interesting for the duration.
reviews.conditions: Mixed ice and rock, moderate wind, cold but manageable

routes.summary: A less-traveled alternative ridge offering more shelter from wind than the northeast ridge, but requiring navigation through the dangerous Dhaulagiri Icefall approach.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The Dhaulagiri Icefall is a serious objective hazard that must be navigated quickly. The ridge offers more wind shelter than the northeast ridge but mixed climbing sections add technical difficulty. Multiple camps are needed on the ridge. Very little traffic means self-sufficiency is essential.

routes.name: Northeast Face (Normal Route)
routes.description: The standard route on the world's eighth highest peak, approached via the Manaslu Glacier and northeast face. First climbed by a Japanese expedition in 1956. Has become increasingly popular as an alternative to Everest for commercial expeditions. The route involves glacier travel and moderate snow climbing.

reviews.title: The new popular 8000er
reviews.body: Manaslu has exploded in popularity as an Everest training peak. The normal route is not technically demanding but the altitude and avalanche risk are real. The summit plateau in clouds is disorienting. A solid introduction to 8000m climbing.
reviews.conditions: Autumn weather with some snow, moderate wind, good conditions above Camp 3

routes.summary: The increasingly popular standard route on the eighth highest peak, used as Everest training with moderate snow climbing but serious avalanche and serac hazards above Camp 3.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Restricted area permit also required. Apply at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The serac above Camp 3 is a serious and unavoidable objective hazard that has caused fatalities. The summit plateau is broad and featureless making GPS navigation essential in poor visibility. Avalanche risk is particularly high during autumn snowfall. Increasing commercial popularity means crowding on the normal route during peak season.

routes.name: South Face
routes.description: A direct and steep line up the massive south face. First climbed in 1984. The face features sustained steep ice and mixed terrain with significant avalanche and serac danger. A serious Himalayan objective attempted only by elite alpinists.

Spring season may offer more consolidated snow conditions than autumn

Sustained steep ice on the face

reviews.title: Serious Himalayan face climbing
reviews.body: The south face of Manaslu is massive and intimidating. We climbed fast over two days in a rare weather window. The ice was sustained at 55-60 degrees for thousands of feet. The constant threat of avalanche from above never lets you relax.
reviews.conditions: Consolidated spring snow, cold, stable weather window

routes.summary: A direct and serious face route with sustained steep ice at 55-60 degrees, attempted only by elite alpinists in fast alpine style to minimize avalanche exposure.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Massive avalanche exposure on the face demands a fast alpine-style approach. Serac barriers present unpredictable collapse risk throughout the ascent. Sustained 55-60 degree ice for thousands of feet requires excellent ice climbing endurance. Spring may offer more consolidated snow conditions than the standard autumn season.

routes.name: East Pinnacle Route
routes.description: A route via the East Pinnacle and main summit ridge. The pinnacle offers interesting mixed climbing before joining the summit ridge for the final push. Less traveled than the normal route with a more technical character.

reviews.title: A more interesting Manaslu

reviews.conditions: Good mixed conditions on pinnacle, wind on summit ridge

routes.summary: A more technical alternative to Manaslu's normal route via the East Pinnacle, offering engaging mixed climbing before an exposed and corniced traverse to the main summit.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The traverse from the East Pinnacle to the main summit is exposed and heavily corniced. Mixed climbing on the pinnacle demands more technical skill than the normal route. Cornice collapse risk on the summit ridge requires careful route finding. Wind exposure on the summit traverse can be extreme.

routes.name: Rakhiot Face (Normal Route)
routes.description: The original 1953 route via the Rakhiot Glacier and face. Hermann Buhl's legendary solo first ascent summit day covering the final 1300m alone in 41 hours is one of mountaineering's greatest achievements. The route follows the Rakhiot Glacier to Silbersattel then traverses to the summit.

reviews.title: Following in Buhl's footsteps
reviews.body: Climbing the Rakhiot route knowing that Buhl soloed the summit push in 1953 is humbling. The face is enormous and the summit day from high camp is brutal. The mountain's reputation as Killer Mountain is well earned. Nanga Parbat demands your absolute best.
reviews.conditions: Stable July weather, firm snow on face, cold summit night

routes.summary: The historic original route of Hermann Buhl's legendary 1953 solo first ascent, ascending the massive Rakhiot Face via the Silbersattel with a brutally long summit day.

The summit day from high camp is extremely long and Buhl's 41-hour push shows the potential for epic. Unpredictable weather on Nanga Parbat can trap climbers high. The mountain has one of the highest fatality rates among 8000m peaks.

routes.name: Diamir Face (Kinshofer Route)
routes.description: The most popular modern route approaching from the Diamir (west) side. Named after the 1962 first ascent team led by Kinshofer. The Kinshofer Wall at 6100m is the technical crux with steep ice climbing. The route then follows a long traverse to the summit.

Fixed ropes are usually in place on the Kinshofer Wall during the season

reviews.title: The modern standard on Nanga Parbat
reviews.body: The Diamir Face is the most practical route on Nanga Parbat. The Kinshofer Wall is an exciting piece of steep ice climbing. Above the wall the route is long and committing with a multi-day traverse to the summit. A serious 8000m objective.
reviews.conditions: Good ice on Kinshofer Wall, variable weather above, cold summit push

routes.summary: The most popular modern route on Nanga Parbat, featuring the technical Kinshofer Wall at 6100m followed by a long exposed traverse to the summit.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $5,400 per climber for Nanga Parbat. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The Kinshofer Wall is steep ice at 60-70 degrees and the primary technical crux of the route. The long traverse above the wall to the summit is exposed and committing. Serac danger exists on multiple sections of the Diamir Face. Fixed ropes are usually present on the Kinshofer Wall during the season but should not be relied upon.

routes.name: Rupal Face (Schell Route)
routes.description: The Rupal Face is the largest mountain face in the world at 4600m from base to summit. First climbed by Reinhold and Gunther Messner in 1970 in an epic ascent that ended with Gunther's death on the descent. The face is enormous with steep ice fields and rock bands.

reviews.title: The biggest wall on Earth
reviews.body: Standing at the base of the Rupal Face and looking up is a life-changing moment. The face just goes up forever. Four days of climbing through ice fields and rock bands in total commitment. The Messner tragedy hangs over every attempt. This is mountaineering at its most serious.
reviews.conditions: Variable conditions, ice fields in good shape, afternoon cloud and spindrift

routes.summary: The largest mountain face on Earth at 4600m, first climbed by the Messner brothers in a tragic 1970 epic, demanding multiple bivouacs on a colossal wall of ice and rock.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $5,400 per climber for Nanga Parbat. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The Rupal Face at 4600m is the largest mountain face on Earth requiring 3-5 planned bivouacs. Avalanche danger from the entire face above is constant and the scale makes escape impossible once committed. The Messner tragedy on the first ascent underscores the extreme commitment required. Alpine style with ultralight bivouac gear is the modern approach but demands exceptional speed and fitness.

routes.name: Mazeno Ridge
routes.description: The longest ridge in the Himalayas at 13km traversing multiple summits over 7000m before reaching Nanga Parbat's main summit. First completed in 2012 by Sandy Allan and Rick Allen. An extraordinary endurance challenge requiring 7+ days on the ridge above 7000m.

reviews.title: The longest ridge in the Himalayas
reviews.body: The Mazeno Ridge redefines what is possible in the mountains. Perhaps the greatest single route achievement in the Himalayas.

routes.summary: The longest ridge in the Himalayas at 13km, requiring over a week above 7000m to traverse multiple summits before reaching Nanga Parbat's main peak.

Once committed to the ridge there is no practical escape route. The 2012 first complete traverse by Allan and Allen is one of modern mountaineering's greatest achievements. Ultralight expedition gear optimized for 7+ days of self-sufficiency is mandatory.

Every step above base camp feels consequential. Herzog and Lachenal's 1950 first ascent was an act of extraordinary courage.

routes.summary: The historic first 8000m route ever climbed, summited by Herzog and Lachenal in 1950, with deceptively moderate terrain hiding the highest fatality-to-summit ratio of any 8000er.

routes.name: South Face

reviews.title: The face that changed Himalayan climbing

routes.summary: One of the most dangerous and technically demanding faces in the Himalayas, first climbed by Bonington's 1970 expedition through 3000m of near-vertical rock, ice, and seracs.

routes.name: East Ridge

reviews.conditions: Variable winds, mixed conditions, cold nights on ridge

routes.summary: A long ridge route approaching through the scenic Annapurna Sanctuary, traversing multiple sub-summits with less avalanche threat than the faces but extreme length and commitment.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members), plus $200 for each additional member. Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The ridge is extremely long with multiple sub-summits adding days to the climb. Wind exposure along the ridge can be extreme and sustained. Multiple camps on the ridge create complex logistics. The approach through the Annapurna Sanctuary is well-established but the ridge above is committing.

routes.name: Japanese Couloir (Normal Route)
routes.description: The standard route first climbed in 1958 by an American expedition. The route ascends through the South Gasherbrum Glacier to a prominent couloir on the south face. The couloir is steep and often icy, providing the technical crux of the climb. Also known as Hidden Peak due to its position deep in the Karakoram.
routes.hazards: ["Steep icy couloir","Rockfall","Altitude","Remote location in Karakoram","Crevassed approach"]

tips.content: The couloir is often hard ice requiring solid front-pointing technique
Gasherbrum I shares base camp with G2, many teams attempt both peaks
July to August offers the best weather window in the Karakoram

gear.notes: Hard ice in the couloir requires stiff technical crampons
For the steep couloir sections

reviews.title: Hidden Peak earned its name
reviews.body: Gasherbrum I is hidden deep in the Karakoram and reaching base camp is an adventure in itself. The Japanese Couloir is a fine piece of ice climbing at altitude. The summit views across the Karakoram giants are unmatched. A hidden gem among the 8000ers.
reviews.conditions: Good ice in couloir, clear summit day, moderate cold

routes.summary: The standard route on Hidden Peak deep in the Karakoram, featuring a steep and often icy couloir as the technical crux, with many teams combining it with a Gasherbrum II attempt.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $4,500 per climber for Gasherbrum I. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The couloir is often hard ice requiring solid front-pointing technique and reliable crampon systems. Rockfall in the couloir is a significant hazard especially in afternoon warming. The remote Karakoram location means rescue capability is extremely limited. Many teams attempt both GI and GII from the same base camp to maximize acclimatization.

routes.name: Northwest Face
routes.description: First climbed by Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler in alpine style in 1975, this was a landmark ascent in Himalayan climbing. The route climbs directly up the northwest face with steep ice and mixed terrain. A milestone in the shift toward lightweight alpine-style climbing on 8000m peaks.
routes.hazards: ["Steep face climbing","Avalanche risk","No fixed ropes","Storm exposure","Altitude"]

tips.content: Messner and Habeler climbed this in alpine style in 1975, setting a new standard for 8000m climbing
Alpine style means total self-sufficiency, no fixed ropes or stocked camps

gear.notes: Weight is critical for alpine style on an 8000m face
Planned and unplanned bivouacs on the face

reviews.title: Alpine style on an 8000er
reviews.body: Following the Messner-Habeler line in alpine style is a statement of intent. No fixed ropes, no stocked camps, just you and the mountain. The northwest face is steep and committing. This route changed Himalayan climbing forever.
reviews.conditions: Good neve on face, brief weather window, cold bivouac

routes.summary: A landmark alpine-style route first climbed by Messner and Habeler in 1975, marking a revolutionary shift toward lightweight fast ascents on 8000m peaks.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $4,500 per climber for Gasherbrum I. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: Alpine style means total self-sufficiency with no fixed ropes or pre-stocked camps. The steep face is exposed to avalanche risk requiring careful timing with weather windows. Planned and unplanned bivouacs on the face require reliable ultralight shelter. This route demands exceptional fitness and prior 8000m experience.

routes.name: West Spur (Normal Route)
routes.description: The standard route first climbed by an Austrian team including Hermann Buhl in 1957 without supplemental oxygen or high-altitude porters. The route follows the broad west spur with moderate snow and rock climbing. The summit plateau is famously long and exposed with multiple sub-summits.
routes.hazards: ["Long exposed summit plateau","Wind on west spur","Altitude","Crevassed approach","Multiple false summits"]

tips.content: The summit plateau has multiple bumps and the true summit is the farthest one
Many teams combine Broad Peak with GI or GII from the same base camp
The west spur was first climbed without oxygen or porters, a bold ascent for 1957

gear.notes: Long summit day on exposed plateau requires full protection

links.productName: Mountain Hardwear Absolute Zero Down Suit

gear.notes: Multiple summits on plateau require navigation in poor visibility

reviews.title: The accessible Karakoram 8000er
reviews.body: Broad Peak is considered one of the more straightforward 8000m peaks but the summit plateau is deceiving. It goes on and on with false summits. The true summit is far and by the time you get there you are exhausted. Do not underestimate this mountain. Buhl's oxygenless ascent was remarkable.
reviews.conditions: Clear approach, wind on upper spur, long but clear summit day

routes.summary: The standard route first climbed without oxygen by Buhl's 1957 team, featuring a deceptively long summit plateau with multiple false summits that has caught out many climbers.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $4,500 per climber for Broad Peak. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The summit plateau has multiple bumps and the true summit is the farthest one; many climbers turn back at false summits. GPS navigation is essential on the featureless plateau in poor visibility. Wind exposure on the west spur can be extreme. Many teams combine Broad Peak with GI or GII attempts from the same base camp area.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: An alternative route from the Chinese side via the north ridge. Steeper and more technical than the standard west spur. The ridge involves mixed climbing and exposed traverses. Rarely attempted due to access from China.
routes.hazards: ["Technical mixed climbing","Exposed ridge","Chinese access required","Isolation from other teams"]

tips.content: Chinese-side access requires separate permits and logistics
The north ridge is more technical than the west spur but avoids the long summit plateau

gear.notes: Technical mixed sections on the ridge
gear.specificProduct: Black Diamond Mixed Climbing Rack Package

gear.notes: Must be self-sufficient with all rope and anchors

reviews.title: Broad Peak from the back
reviews.body: The north ridge is a completely different experience from the standard route. More technical climbing on mixed terrain with incredible exposure. The ridge approach from China is remote and adds to the adventure. A fine mountaineering route.
reviews.conditions: Mixed conditions on ridge, variable weather, cold

routes.summary: A rarely attempted technical alternative from K2's Chinese side, offering steeper mixed climbing and greater isolation but avoiding the notoriously long summit plateau.
routes.permitInfo: Chinese Mountaineering Association (CMA) permit required for north side access. Fee approximately $10,000-$15,000 per climber. Must book through authorized Chinese operator. Apply at least 12 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: Chinese-side access requires separate and more expensive permits with longer lead times. Complete self-sufficiency is required as there are no other teams on this route. Technical mixed climbing on the ridge demands strong alpine skills. Isolation from other expeditions means no external rescue capability.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge (Normal Route)
routes.description: The standard route and often considered the easiest 8000m peak after Cho Oyu. First climbed in 1956 by an Austrian expedition. The route follows the southwest ridge with moderate snow slopes. Popular as an acclimatization peak before attempting K2 or Gasherbrum I from the same base camp.
routes.hazards: ["Altitude","Crevassed glacier approach","Wind on upper ridge","Serac band at 7000m"]

tips.content: GII shares base camp with GI and K2, many climbers combine multiple peaks in one trip
Often done as a warmup for K2, the summit success rate is high
The serac band at 7000m must be passed quickly as it is actively calving

gear.notes: Crampons, ice axe, and harness sufficient for the moderate terrain
Full down suit optional, many climb in down jacket and pants

reviews.title: The gentle giant of the Karakoram
reviews.body: GII is the most approachable of the Karakoram 8000ers. The southwest ridge is a steady moderate climb. Used this as acclimatization before a K2 attempt. The summit panorama with K2 looming above and the Karakoram stretching in all directions is breathtaking.
reviews.conditions: Good snow conditions, moderate wind, clear summit day

routes.summary: Often considered the easiest 8000m peak after Cho Oyu, popular as an acclimatization climb before K2 attempts, with a dangerous serac band at 7000m as the main hazard.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $4,500 per climber for Gasherbrum II. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The serac band at 7000m must be passed quickly as it is actively calving and presents unavoidable objective danger. Despite being considered easier, GII is still an 8000m peak with all associated altitude risks. The crevassed glacier approach requires careful roped travel. Wind on the upper ridge can be fierce and unpredictable.

routes.name: Northwest Face
routes.description: A direct line up the northwest face offering a more challenging alternative to the standard route. Steeper ice and mixed terrain with less infrastructure. Attempted in alpine style by strong teams seeking a more demanding experience on GII.
routes.hazards: ["Steep ice","Avalanche risk on face","No fixed ropes","Altitude"]

tips.content: The northwest face provides a much steeper and more engaging climb than the normal route
Best attempted by teams acclimatized from other Karakoram peaks first

gear.notes: Steep ice face requires aggressive tools
Protection on the steep face

reviews.title: GII the hard way
reviews.body: The northwest face transforms GII from a moderate snow peak into a genuine alpine challenge. Steep sustained ice climbing at 7000m plus. Far more satisfying than the standard route. A great face climb for teams stepping up from alpine objectives.
reviews.conditions: Good ice on face, cold, brief weather window

routes.summary: A steeper and more engaging alternative to GII's standard route, offering sustained ice climbing at 7000m+ best attempted by teams already acclimatized on nearby Karakoram peaks.
routes.permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required. Royalty fee approximately $4,500 per climber for Gasherbrum II. Apply through licensed Pakistani expedition operator at least 6 months in advance. Liaison officer mandatory.
routes.safetyNotes: The steep ice face has no fixed ropes requiring full self-sufficiency in protection placement. Avalanche risk on the face demands careful timing with stable weather windows. Best attempted by teams already acclimatized from other Karakoram peaks. Brief weather windows in the Karakoram mean speed is essential.

routes.name: North Ridge (Normal Route)
routes.description: The standard route on the lowest of the fourteen 8000m peaks approached entirely from Tibet. First climbed by a large Chinese expedition in 1964. The route follows moderate snow slopes along the north ridge. Many teams reach only the Central Summit at 8008m rather than the true summit which requires an exposed traverse.
routes.hazards: ["Exposed summit traverse to true summit","Altitude","Wind on ridge","Crevassed glacier","Chinese permit logistics"]

tips.content: The Central Summit at 8008m and the true summit at 8027m are separated by an exposed traverse
Many claimed ascents are actually only to the Central Summit, not the true high point
Shishapangma is the only 8000er entirely within Tibet, Chinese permits required
Spring season April to May offers the best conditions

gear.notes: The normal route is technically straightforward
gear.specificProduct: Petzl Summit Evo Axe + Grivel G12 Crampons

links.productName: Petzl Summit Evo + Grivel G12 Bundle

gear.notes: For summit day and the exposed traverse to the true summit

links.productName: Mountain Hardwear Absolute Zero Down Suit

reviews.title: The forgotten 8000er
reviews.body: Shishapangma gets less attention than other 8000m peaks but the north ridge is a fine climb. The summit traverse to the true summit is exposed and many teams turn back at the Central Summit. We pushed on to the true summit and the ridge walk was the highlight. The last of the 8000ers to be climbed.
reviews.conditions: Clear spring weather, moderate wind, good snow conditions

routes.summary: The standard route on the lowest and last-climbed 8000er, entirely within Tibet, where many teams reach only the Central Summit rather than completing the exposed traverse to the true summit.
routes.permitInfo: Chinese Tibet Mountaineering Association (CTMA) permit required as Shishapangma lies entirely within Tibet. Fee approximately $9,500 per climber. Must book through authorized Chinese operator. Apply at least 8 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The exposed traverse from the Central Summit to the true summit is the most dangerous section and many teams turn back. Many claimed ascents are only to the Central Summit at 8008m, not the true high point at 8027m. Chinese permit logistics require significant advance planning. Wind on the ridge can make the summit traverse extremely hazardous.

routes.name: Southwest Face
routes.description: A direct and serious face route on the Nepali side first climbed in 1982. The southwest face is a large wall of ice and rock with significant objective hazards. Approached from the Langtang region of Nepal, this face has attracted many of the world's best alpinists.
routes.hazards: ["Steep ice and mixed terrain","Avalanche risk","Rockfall","Storm exposure","Altitude"]

tips.content: The Nepali approach provides an alternative to Chinese permits and logistics
Alpine style is the preferred approach for this face given the objective dangers

gear.notes: Steep mixed terrain on the face
Alpine style with planned bivouacs

reviews.title: Shishapangma's serious side
reviews.body: The southwest face reveals a completely different mountain than the gentle north ridge. Steep sustained climbing on ice and rock with serious avalanche exposure. The face has attracted top alpinists for decades and not all have returned. A serious Himalayan objective.
reviews.conditions: Mixed conditions, some ice, brief stable window

routes.summary: A serious face route on the Nepali side first climbed in 1982, featuring steep ice and mixed terrain that has attracted elite alpinists to this otherwise moderate peak.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required for the Nepali approach. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members). Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The Nepali approach avoids Chinese permit complexities but the face itself is a serious alpine objective. Steep ice and mixed terrain demand strong technical climbing skills at altitude. Avalanche and rockfall risk on the face require careful timing. Alpine style is preferred to minimize exposure time on the hazardous face.

routes.name: South Face Direct
routes.description: A direct line up the center of the south face avoiding the couloirs and aiming straight for the summit. First climbed in 2005. More sustained and technical than the southwest face with fewer natural rest points. A modern test piece.
routes.hazards: ["Sustained technical difficulty","Direct avalanche exposure","No retreat from upper face","Altitude"]

tips.content: Autumn can offer better ice conditions on the south face than spring
The direct line is more exposed to objective hazards than the southwest face

gear.notes: Sustained technical climbing requires comprehensive gear
Unplanned bivouacs are likely on this sustained face

reviews.title: Modern alpinism on an 8000er
reviews.body: The south face direct cuts right through the heart of the face. No natural lines or features to follow, just straight up. The climbing is relentless and the exposure is extreme. A route that defines modern Himalayan alpinism.
reviews.conditions: Autumn ice, cold temperatures, stable weather for 3 days

routes.summary: A modern test piece climbing directly up the center of Shishapangma's south face, with sustained technical difficulty and direct avalanche exposure making it a cutting-edge objective.
routes.permitInfo: Nepal Ministry of Tourism permit required for the Nepali approach. Royalty fee: $1,500 per climber (up to 7 members). Apply through licensed expedition operator at least 4 months in advance.
routes.safetyNotes: The direct line is more exposed to objective hazards than the southwest face route. Sustained technical difficulty offers no rest points or escape options from the upper face. Autumn may offer better ice conditions but weather windows are brief. Unplanned bivouacs are likely on this sustained face requiring reliable emergency shelter.
